articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Sunyshore wins the ground game, then takes the fourth-down chance
articles.dek: Myles Gabite rushes for 106 yards, Kobra Khan catches two touchdowns, and the Starseekers hold Hearthome to six points.

body.text: Sunyshore’s most consequential throw came on fourth-and-five with eighteen seconds left in the first half. DeZhaun Watzon found Kobra Khan short left for a seventeen-yard touchdown, turning a 7–6 lead into a 13–6 halftime advantage. The Starseekers had backed their offense to finish the possession, and it did. They never allowed another Hearthome point, winning 23–6 to earn a divisional home game against Petalburg.

Myles Gabite supplied the game’s most consistent offensive work, carrying fifteen times for 106 yards and a touchdown. Sunyshore gained 143 rushing yards while holding Hearthome to nineteen. Watzon threw two touchdowns, both to Kobra Khan, and took no sacks. That combination gave the Starseekers several ways to maintain control even when their passing yardage was modest.

I picked Sunyshore, and the defensive part of the argument held up. Hearthome managed eight first downs and 175 total yards. Its one touchdown briefly made the game close in the second quarter, but the Haunts could not build a running game or sustain enough passing offense to keep threatening. The Starseekers did not need a spectacular quarterback line to advance. They needed useful completions, a productive ground attack and a defense that kept answering.
The fourth-down throw changed halftime

body.speaker: Karson Jones
body.text: Myles gave us the kind of work you can build a whole afternoon around. The defense gave us time to keep doing it. We earned another home game, and now Petalburg gets our attention. The crowd can enjoy this one while we prepare for the next one.

Myles Gabite opened the scoring with a two-yard run up the middle at 2:31 of the first quarter. Kayden Lyons made the extra point, giving Sunyshore a 7–0 lead. Hearthome replied in the second quarter when Frosmoth found Haunter deep left for a twenty-one-yard touchdown at 3:37. The missed extra point left the score 7–6, close enough for the next scoring opportunity to carry real weight.

Sunyshore’s late-half possession reached fourth-and-five. Watzon’s short-left throw to Kobra Khan went seventeen yards for the touchdown at 0:18. The extra point failed, but the Starseekers still took a seven-point lead into halftime. The decision to keep the offense on the field produced six points and made Hearthome’s otherwise competitive first half end with a more difficult second-half assignment.

Kobra Khan would score again in the fourth quarter on a short-right completion recorded in the play log as eighteen yards. The game’s receiving table credits him with two catches, thirty-four yards and two touchdowns, with a listed long of seventeen; the play descriptions and aggregate yardage differ by one yard. The touchdowns agree across both records. We retain the official table and recorded descriptions as supplied rather than inventing a correction.

The larger point is unaffected by that small reporting discrepancy. Both of the receiver’s catches ended in touchdowns. Fera LaGatr did the heavier receiving work between those moments, catching nine of ten targets for eighty-seven yards. Sunyshore had a frequent completion available and a separate receiver who finished its two passing scores. Watzon completed eighteen of thirty attempts for 164 yards without an interception.

body.alt: Arbok #19. Kobra Khan caught both of Sunyshore’s touchdown passes. Editorial receiving illustration.
body.caption: Kobra Khan caught both of Sunyshore’s touchdown passes. Editorial receiving illustration.

body.text: Gabite kept the offense in workable situations

The Garchomp wearing number 99 averaged just over seven yards per carry. His longest run gained seventeen yards, so the 106-yard total was built through repeated useful attempts rather than one enormous breakaway. BAXXED? added thirty-one yards on six carries. Watzon and Jolt Vick contributed short rushing gains as well, giving Sunyshore twenty-three carries for 143 yards.

That production mattered against an opponent whose own ground game could not stay productive. Gumshoos carried seven times for seven yards. Palafin gained nine on three attempts, and Litleo gained four on three. Hearthome finished with nineteen rushing yards on fourteen carries. Its longest individual run was six yards. The Haunts repeatedly needed their passing game to supply distance that Sunyshore could obtain on the ground.

Gabite’s last three runs also helped finish the game. After Hearthome’s late interception, he gained five yards up the middle, six to the right and twelve to the left. Those carries used the remaining time and secured the result without requiring another pass. The final sequence is a useful illustration of what the running game had provided throughout the afternoon: gains large enough to change the next down and reduce the number of chances Hearthome would receive.

Karson Jones has a straightforward strength to carry into the next round. Sunyshore can ask its passing game to make important plays without asking it to supply every productive yard. That does not make the rushing output automatic against Petalburg. It gives the Pride a concrete problem to prepare for after a wild-card game in which Rustboro ran for 163 yards against them.
Hearthome’s passing game needed more help

Frosmoth completed sixteen of twenty-three passes for 156 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Abomasnow caught six of seven targets for eighty yards; Castform added four catches for thirty-four. Haunter’s touchdown accounted for most of his twenty-three receiving yards. The completion rate was respectable, but the offense did not create enough first downs or explosive gains to offset its limited rushing production.

Sunyshore sacked Frosmoth three times. Vigoroth recorded two of them, including a seven-yard loss with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter. Anorith supplied the other, a third-and-seven sack in the third. Those plays helped interrupt the possessions Hearthome needed to keep the score manageable. The Starseekers’ own quarterback finished without a sack taken, a substantial difference in an afternoon with relatively few total passing yards.

The Haunts also left kicking points behind. Sunflora missed the extra point following Haunter’s touchdown and missed the team’s only field-goal attempt. Those misses do not account for a seventeen-point defeat, but they reduced the reward for the limited scoring opportunities Hearthome created. Sunyshore’s Lyons made a fifty-six-yard field goal at 0:51 of the third quarter, extending the lead to 16–6 despite his earlier missed extra point.

body.alt: Porygon-Z #30. DeZhaun Watzon threw two touchdowns without an interception. Imagined postgame portrait.
body.caption: DeZhaun Watzon threw two touchdowns without an interception. Imagined postgame portrait.

body.text: Kobra Khan’s second touchdown came at 2:28 of the fourth. Lyons made that extra point, and Sunyshore led 23–6. On the following Hearthome possession, the Vigoroth sack was followed by an interception: Frosmoth threw deep left on third-and-eleven, and Sunyshore’s number 12 Ampharos returned the ball seventeen yards. Gabite’s final three carries then closed the game.
Petalburg brings a different late-game test

Hearthome entered at 8–8–1 and reached the playoffs through a crowded wild-card race. Its visit to Sunyshore ended with one touchdown and no second-half points. The full season accounting belongs in the offseason issue. For this elimination game, the record shows a defense that could not fully contain Gabite and an offense that lacked enough rushing support to keep challenging after halftime.

Sunyshore entered at 13–4 and now has a postseason win to accompany its division title. The Starseekers produced sixteen first downs, converted five of ten third downs and punted only once. Their offense ran fifty-three plays to Hearthome’s forty. Those measures support the result without requiring a claim that every part of the performance was polished. Watzon still had twelve incompletions, and the kicking unit missed an extra point.

Petalburg arrives after converting six of nine third downs and scoring twenty-one fourth-quarter points against Rustboro. That is a different challenge from Hearthome’s afternoon. Sunyshore will need to finish possessions against a quarterback who just made two difficult third-down throws on a go-ahead drive. Its own rushing attack has an inviting recent comparison, but the Pride have already shown they can win despite allowing substantial ground production.

The availability report also carries forward. 88 Special remains listed for fifteen weeks, while Serp Gardener, Nair Jordan and BJ Vickers have new minor entries with no remaining absence. Those zero-week entries do not establish an injury-related missed start. Sunyshore can prepare from its confirmed healthy options while continuing to account for the ongoing absence. The team’s next step is a home divisional game, with a running back in productive form and a defense that just allowed six points.

articles.author: ellis-quill
articles.title: Watchog finishes the drives Eterna cannot
articles.dek: Two five-yard touchdown runs and a late interception send Dewford to Mossdeep with a 20–9 road win.

body.text: Watchog scored from five yards out in the first quarter, then did it again in the second. Eterna answered with field goals. That distinction lasted the whole afternoon: Dewford reached the end zone twice, the Thorns never did, and the Breakers won 20–9 to earn a divisional trip to undefeated Mossdeep. A game with nearly equal total yardage turned on what each offense could do when points became available.

Dewford gained 225 yards to Eterna’s 232. Both teams recorded twelve first downs and threw one interception. Neither lost a fumble. The Breakers nevertheless led 14–0 before Eterna scored, then used two fourth-quarter field goals and Carnivine’s late interception to protect the advantage. The Thorns’ defensive reputation remained visible in stretches. Their offense could not produce the touchdown required to give that defense a winning margin.

I tend to distrust conclusions built from one afternoon, particularly when the conclusion tries to erase eleven regular-season wins. Eterna’s 11–6 season contained enough useful football to earn a home playoff game. This game supplied a narrower verdict: against Dewford, the Thorns converted one of eight third downs and settled for three field goals. Their season ended before the offense could change that pattern.
Dewford recovered from the first mistake

body.speaker: Brawly
body.text: Watchog finished the two chances near the goal line, and the defense kept making them kick. That gave us a game we could manage. Mossdeep is a different assignment, and the work starts with understanding what we will need to do better on the next trip.

The Breakers’ opening passing possession included an interception. Frosmoth threw deep left on third-and-five at 4:24 of the first quarter, and Eterna’s Gliscor returned it nineteen yards. An early road turnover could have given the Thorns the kind of low-scoring lead they preferred. Eterna did not turn it into points, and Dewford subsequently found the first touchdown.

Watchog ran right for five yards at 0:47. The extra point made it 7–0. His second touchdown came on another five-yard run, this time left, at 2:58 of the second quarter. Dewford led 14–0 after the kick. Watchog finished with seven carries for twenty-seven yards and two touchdowns, a line that makes more sense when the scoring opportunities are kept attached to the modest yardage total.

Excadrill supplied the larger share of the rushing workload, carrying sixteen times for sixty-four yards. Meowscarada gained twenty-one on two attempts, while Kricketune added five on four. Dewford finished with thirty carries for 120 yards. The Breakers did not overwhelm Eterna with a succession of long runs; they used enough productive rushing work to reach two short touchdown opportunities and then completed both.

That approach also limited what Frosmoth had to supply after the interception. He completed eleven of sixteen attempts for 105 yards, no touchdowns and one pick. Machoke caught five of six targets for thirty-two yards. Swellow added twenty-eight on two catches, and Excadrill caught a twenty-yard pass. The quarterback’s afternoon was modest, but it did not need to resemble Hatterene’s five-touchdown performance elsewhere in the bracket.

body.alt: Excadrill #46. Excadrill carried sixteen times for sixty-four yards. Editorial rushing illustration.
body.caption: Excadrill carried sixteen times for sixty-four yards. Editorial rushing illustration.

body.text: Eterna’s kicker kept the game available

Vikavolt made a fifty-seven-yard field goal at 1:52 of the second quarter, putting Eterna on the board. He added a twenty-four-yarder three seconds before halftime. The Thorns went to the interval trailing 14–6, close enough that a touchdown and a successful two-point try could have tied the game. Their kicker had converted both opportunities, including the unusually long first attempt.

The next Eterna score was another field goal. Slowking was sacked for seven yards on third-and-three at 2:56 of the third quarter, and Vikavolt made the forty-one-yard attempt eighteen seconds later. Dewford’s lead was down to 14–9. The Thorns had scored on three possessions without reaching the end zone, which kept the game close while leaving the offense with the same unfinished task.

Dewford answered in the fourth quarter with a forty-seven-yard field goal at 5:22. The score became 17–9, requiring Eterna to produce a touchdown and two-point conversion merely to draw level. The Breakers’ kicker is now listed as Camerupt in the box score; the recorded play descriptions retain Numel, the form used in the game. The identity is consistent even though the later display name reflects progression.

That distinction is small compared with the competitive one. Both kickers were perfect on field goals: Dewford two for two, Eterna three for three. The Thorns could not ask their kicker to solve a touchdown deficit by missing fewer kicks. He had already made all of them. Their offense needed to reach the end zone, and the Breakers repeatedly prevented that final step.
The interception that protected the final minutes

Eterna began another fourth-quarter possession with Slowking taking a seven-yard sack from Infernape. The Thorns continued trying to move the ball, but at 2:20 Slowking’s deep throw left was intercepted by Carnivine and returned sixteen yards. Dewford had the ball, an eight-point lead and a chance to use the remaining time while moving toward a final field goal.

Excadrill gained six yards up the middle at the two-minute warning. Watchog then converted third-and-one with a three-yard run left. The Breakers continued running, and their kicker made a thirty-seven-yard field goal with thirty-four seconds remaining. The lead was 20–9. Eterna now needed two scores with only a brief possession available, and the practical comeback window had closed.

Slowking completed a fifteen-yard fourth-down pass to Cramorant near the end, but it came too late to change the score. He finished eleven of twenty-four for 148 yards, with no touchdowns, one interception and two sacks taken. Trevenant led the receivers with fifty-eight yards on four catches. Marowak added forty-seven on three. Eterna had individual completions that moved the ball; it could not connect enough of them into a touchdown drive.

body.alt: Slowking #12. Eterna finished without a touchdown. Imagined postgame scene with Slowking.
body.caption: Eterna finished without a touchdown. Imagined postgame scene with Slowking.

body.text: Whiscash carried sixteen times for sixty-six yards, and Dodrio added eighteen on three attempts. The Thorns’ eighty-four rushing yards were useful without being decisive. When the offense reached third down, it converted only once in eight tries. Dewford converted four of eleven. Neither rate suggests an effortless offensive afternoon, but the Breakers found enough extra possessions and enough finishing plays to make the difference.
Mossdeep is familiar, and the assignment is larger

Dewford’s next opponent won all seventeen regular-season games, yet the Breakers have a specific reason to approach the trip with more than generic underdog optimism. They lost 24–21 to Mossdeep in Week 4. That result shows they previously kept a meeting close. It does not establish that the same sequence will repeat months of development and several roster decisions later, but it gives the preview an actual competitive history.

The wild-card win also follows Dewford’s 35–29 victory at Rustboro in the regular-season finale. The Breakers have advanced through two different kinds of games: a high-scoring finale featuring a major return play, then a more restrained road playoff game decided by rushing touchdowns and defensive stops. Their next opponent will have to prepare for both the return threat and the offense’s willingness to keep working through a running game.

Mossdeep’s own late-season results came with confirmed coaching intent to rest starters and give younger players opportunities. The Eclipse’s divisional personnel should be judged from what is actually selected, rather than assumed from those finale lineups. Dewford, meanwhile, has a new minor entry for Dusclops with zero weeks remaining and no positive-week injury listed among its current players. That gives the Breakers a comparatively clean availability report entering the trip.

Eterna leaves with a defense that kept the game within reach and an offense that never supplied the necessary touchdown. Dewford leaves with Watchog’s two finishes, Excadrill’s workload, Carnivine’s interception and a place in the final eight. The next destination is Mossdeep, where the Breakers will need more than a reminder that they once came close. They have earned the opportunity to find out whether this version can complete the job.
